page.items_caption: Every figure, table and number of the paper, with our value and why it differs.
page.claims_line: The direction of the main finding holds on our run: PTC+ junctions and alternative splicing go up far more often than canonical splicing when NMD is lost, and regulated PTCs prefer UGA. We find a quarter of the paper's PTC+ junctions; why is open, and the lost TROMER exon set is the main suspect.
came_back: Up, unchanged and down junctions within 7% in BMM; 2,226 junctions up in both tissues against 2,257.
All 18 stop codon shares within 0.02; UGA preferred in both tissues.
Of the 50 events of Additional file 9, our PTC rule calls 45 and gives the printed distance for 42.
Alternative junctions go up about three times as often as canonical ones (BMM 33% against 12%).
buried: RAINMAN's scripts and its junction database are gone.
TROMER, one of the paper's exon sources, has no mouse data online.
The 2011 RefSeq and Ensembl tables are gone; the database is 9% smaller.
The GO analyses need DAVID's 2012 knowledgebase.
page.matched_intro: We matched what the paper and its supplement state:
matched: Bowtie with two mismatches in the first 68 bp, best stratum; truncation in 10-nt steps to 35 nt.
All exon pairs within each RefSeq gene, 4 nt of overlap each side.
Three reads, TMM within each tissue, two-fold change.
Stop more than 49 nt before the last junction.
page.closing: RAINMAN came back as a package. Its PTC counts fall short, and we have not yet shown why.
